quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the front brake pressure. Then re-apply the brake with steady, gradual pressure.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should mirrors be used?

options.text: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
Should be used only by the lead rider.
Should not be checked frequently because they can be a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
questions.explanation: All riders should check mirrors often to watch the riders behind them and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. What clothing should you wear?

options.text: Do not need to wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear brightly-colored clothing when riding to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes oily and slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to other vehicles?

options.text: Need less room to stop than other larger vehicles.
Need as much room to stop as other larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need as much room to stop as other larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need as much stopping distance as other vehicles. Always keep enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how quickly it is consumed. How often a person drinks does not affect their BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you avoid?

options.text: The front and rear brakes need to be used at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to control your speed during the turn.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Clothing that feels comfortable.
Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good motorcycle clothing protects you in a crash. It should also keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
A signal is ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must stop completely. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How quickly does alcohol reach the brain after being consumed?

options.text: Within minutes
About one hour later
About two hours later

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects your riding ability within minutes of drinking. Riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in this area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you space to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material during the day to be seen better. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When holding the handlegrips, how should your arms be positioned?

options.text: Bent a lot at the elbow.
Slightly bent at the elbow.
Fully extended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly bent at the elbow.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlegrips. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you push on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: What can happen if you grab the front brake or jam the rear brake?

options.text: The brakes can lock.
It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes can lock.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can lock the brakes. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: Changes in the road surface ahead.
Traffic around you.
Conditions that stay the same as you approach.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you approach.
questions.explanation: Look ahead for potential problems on the road. Make a plan to reduce the risks they create.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves to prevent a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves to prevent a skid.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while you ride over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Exaggerate the zigzag motion to alert other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings. Do not try to correct the weaving by leaning side to side. This zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not ride between stopped or slow-moving vehicles. Other vehicles may change lanes, open doors, or extend arms out windows. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to ride safely.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Stacked against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over the rear axle or in front of it. Only experienced riders should carry loads on motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while you are stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Keep applying the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the brake immediately and then re-apply it firmly. Use both front and rear brakes for quick stops.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can cause what problem?

options.text: Be helpful in most situations.
Improve steering.
Cause control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locked brakes cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it right away. If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Only a few minutes.
About an hour.
It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcyclists?

options.text: Sneakers.
Sturdy boots.
Sandals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet best. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What can allow moped users to use a bike path?

options.text: Permission from property owners next to the path
Local law
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Local law
questions.explanation: Mopeds and motorized bicycles cannot use bike paths, trails, or equestrian paths unless they are on or next to a road. However, local law may allow these vehicles to use certain trails or roadways.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Keep safe following distances.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe following distances.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe following distances.
